svg.title: Bindings and languages
svg.desc: A physical stack distinguishes the native core, the generated bridge contract, and each package surface.

text.tspan: One core. One bridge contract. Seven surfaces.

g.title: Rust · direct crate
g.desc: Rust callers bypass the bridge and call the implementation directly.

g.title: JavaScript / TypeScript · WASM
g.desc: The browser and Node surfaces share generated names plus byte and JSON contracts.

g.title: Python · nanobind
g.desc: Python objects wrap the native core through a generated, typed extension surface.

g.title: Kotlin · JNA
g.desc: JVM callers load the shared library and use generated symbol and payload definitions.

g.title: PHP · FFI
g.desc: PHP binds the stable C ABI at runtime without a hand-maintained parallel API.

g.title: C · stable headers
g.desc: The C ABI is the lowest common contract used by foreign-language packages.

g.title: C++ · typed wrappers
g.desc: RAII and native types wrap the generated C symbols without duplicating the core.

text.tspan: The annotated bridge owns naming and transport contracts; native Rust remains a direct call path.
